core_obligations: Translate cohomology into torsors over X (proof lines 16140-16146): an element of H^1(X_etale, M) corresponds to an M-torsor F on X_etale; such a torsor is a finite locally constant sheaf, hence is representable by a scheme V finite etale over X, and conversely an M-torsor structure on such a scheme gives a cohomology class.
Do the same over the closed fibre (proof lines 16146-16149): the same translation identifies the cohomology classes over X_0 with the M-torsors which are finite etale over X_0.

Apply the equivalence of categories (proof lines 16149-16152): the equivalence between finite etale covers of X and of X_0 supplied by the theory of the fundamental group for proper schemes over a henselian local ring, compatible with the M-actions, identifies the two sets of torsors and hence the two cohomology groups.
proof_roadmap: Identify cohomology classes with torsors and then with finite etale schemes with an action of M.
Perform the same identification over the closed fibre.
Use the equivalence of categories of finite etale covers for proper schemes over a henselian local ring.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a henselian local ring A, a proper scheme X over A with closed fibre X_0 and a finite abelian group M, the first etale cohomology groups of X and of X_0 with coefficients in the constant sheaf M agree (statement lines 16133-16138). The proof (proof lines 16140-16154) translates both sides into torsors finite etale over the respective schemes and concludes by the equivalence of categories of finite etale covers for proper schemes over a henselian local ring. H2: a two-sided translation with three inputs, written out in full.
